# Three-layer boundary valuations: horizontal PSD divergence plus actual midpoint terms
boundary martingale. It supplies the precise decomposition requested by
the signed-Euler route. It does not construct that martingale from a
below-OC cap menu, and it does not prove a new Gamma payment.

The rational-template boundary-martingale factorization in
`candidate 7959b9ecad75ca36` already
provides the broad two-stage principle. The additional content here is an
explicit three-layer pointwise-pair refinement, its horizontal PSD
second-divergence formula with coefficient 1/2, and exact discrete and
continuous variance budgets. The nonsymmetric test below occurs on actual
compatible supporting faces; its signed measures are not claimed to be
a realized equal-critical cap profile.

## 1. Actual geometry and input hypothesis

Let K_-,K_0,K_+ be compact convex fibers at bases -1,0,1, with

    (K_-+K_+)/2 subset K_0.

Fix a continuous unit normal u, let h_p=h_(K_p)(u), and let
F_p={x in K_p:u.x=h_p}. Let nu and eta be equal-mass finite nonnegative
measures supported on the three lifted faces {p} x F_p. Suppose gamma
is a martingale coupling from nu to eta in BOTH the base and continuous
coordinates. Thus its conditional target mean at input (p,x) is (p,x).

This is exactly the type of fixed-normal convex-order certificate
furnished conditionally by the archived shared-facet critical-roof dual.
It is an input here, not inferred from affine moments alone.

## 2. The nonnegative decomposition theorem

There exist:

* a finite PSD matrix-valued measure A, block-diagonal by base and supported
  on the original continuous faces F_p; and
* a finite nonnegative measure kappa on pairs (y_-,y_+) in F_- x F_+
  whose midpoint m=(y_-+y_+)/2 belongs to F_0,

such that, as signed distributions on the lifted three-layer set,

    nu-eta = - div_x div_x A
              + integral [delta_(0,m)
                    -(1/2)delta_(-1,y_-)-(1/2)delta_(1,y_+)]
                    d kappa(y_-,y_+).                         (1)

Only the CONTINUOUS coordinates are differentiated. There is no diffusion
through noninteger bases. Every discrete term is an actual anchored
lattice midpoint relation, with its exact weights 1/2,1/2. All coefficients
and all matrix measures in (1) are nonnegative in their stated senses.

If phi is concave on the convex hull of these actual faces, (1) gives

    integral phi d(nu-eta)
      = - integral Hess_x(phi):dA
        + integral [phi(0,m)
             -(phi(-1,y_-)+phi(1,y_+))/2] d kappa >=0.          (2)

Thus the sign convention is the correct one for outward CONCAVE roof
velocities. It is not a pointwise positivity assertion about nu-eta.

## 3. Explicit factorization and support proof

Disintegrate gamma at an input a=(p,x). An endpoint input p=1 cannot
send mass to either lower base, because its target base has mean one and
is supported in [-1,1]; similarly at p=-1. Such a row remains in its
own continuous face.

At input p=0, write its probabilities of target bases -1,0,1 as

    a(a), 1-2a(a), a(a),       0<=a(a)<=1/2.

Use the normalized conditional continuous laws at those bases. With
probability 1-2a, draw Y_0 from its target law and set X'=Y_0. With
probability 2a, independently draw Y_- and Y_+ from the two endpoint
conditional laws and set X'=(Y_-+Y_+)/2. Null branches are omitted.
At endpoint inputs simply draw X' from the original target law.

In every row E[X'|p,x]=x, and X' has the SAME base as its input. Let nu'
be the resulting intermediate law, and let kappa be the endpoint-pair
law, including its branch mass 2a. From every pair midpoint, send half
its mass to each endpoint; every other intermediate point stays fixed.
The final law is EXACTLY eta. No original target marginal is altered.

It remains to check the support of the midpoint, rather than assume it.
Compatibility gives (h_-+h_+)/2 <= h_0. The u-coordinate martingale
identity for an input in F_0 gives

    a(h_-+h_+-2h_0)=0.

Therefore every row using an endpoint pair has equality in the support
inequality. Its actual pair midpoint belongs to K_0 by convexity and
has u-coordinate h_0, hence belongs to F_0. The first-stage segment
from x to X' stays inside F_p because F_p is convex.

The construction can be carried out with standard Borel conditional
kernels on compact sets. Independent joining of the two conditional
endpoint laws retains both endpoint marginals. It need not retain an
unspecified preexisting dependence between different outputs, since the
original martingale has only one output per row.

## 4. The PSD measure and its exact coefficient

Let gamma_1 be the first-stage coupling nu -> nu', and put delta=X'-x.
Define A by

    integral B:dA
      = integral_(gamma_1) integral_0^1 (1-t)
          delta^T B(p,x+t delta) delta dt d gamma_1              (3)

for continuous symmetric matrix fields B. For a Borel set E this is
an integral of PSD rank-one matrices delta delta^T with nonnegative
weight (1-t), so A is PSD. Its total trace is finite because the faces
are compact. Its support stays on the actual lifted faces, as above.

Taylor's formula with its integral remainder gives

    phi(p,X')-phi(p,x)
      = grad_x phi(p,x).delta
        + integral_0^1(1-t) delta^T Hess_x phi(p,x+t delta) delta dt.

The first term integrates to zero rowwise. Thus

    nu'-nu = div_x div_x A.                                    (4)

The second stage gives nu'-eta equal to the midpoint integral in (1).
Subtracting (4) proves (1). No integration by parts across a fiber
boundary and no omitted endpoint force is used; these are distributions
on the ambient continuous space with compact support.

## 5. Exact base and continuous variance budgets

The total midpoint mass has an intrinsic formula:

    |kappa| = integral z^2 d eta - integral z^2 d nu.             (5)

Indeed the first stage fixes z. A midpoint atom has z=0 and its two
endpoint outputs have mean square one. Endpoint rows never move in z.
This identity determines the TOTAL amount of arithmetic midpoint work,
independently of the chosen conditional joining.

The PSD part has the exact trace normalization

    2 tr A(total)
       = integral |x|^2 d nu' - integral |x|^2 d nu.             (6)

Here integral_0^1(1-t)dt=1/2. The endpoint splitting adds precisely its
conditional pair variance, so

    integral |x|^2 d eta - integral |x|^2 d nu
      = 2 tr A(total)
         + (1/4) integral |y_+-y_-|^2 d kappa.                  (7)

Every term on the right is nonnegative. In particular, if nu=eta,
(5) gives kappa=0 and (7) gives A=0. The decomposition cannot contain a
nontrivial stationary positive arithmetic cycle hidden by its PSD part.
This is a representation-level version of bounded martingale rigidity,
not a cap-budget estimate.

## 6. A nonsymmetric exact test on actual three-fiber supporting faces

Take C=[-1,1] x T, where T is a triangle having a unit edge parametrized
by s in [0,1]. The three integer fibers are exactly T; every point below
lies on that same actual supporting face, and midpoint compatibility is
exact. Consider

    nu  = delta_(0,3/8),
    eta = (1/2)delta_(-1,0)
           +(1/4)delta_(1,1/2)+(1/4)delta_(1,1).                (8)

Both coordinate means agree. The unique source row is a genuine physical
martingale. Its intermediate law from Section 3 is

    nu'=(1/2)delta_(0,1/4)+(1/2)delta_(0,1/2).

Write J(a,b)=delta_(0,(a+b)/2)
                -(1/2)delta_(-1,a)-(1/2)delta_(1,b).
The exact decomposition is

    nu-eta = -D_s^2 K
               +(1/2)J(0,1/2)+(1/2)J(0,1),                    (9)

where K is the nonnegative continuous-coordinate density at base zero

    K(s)=(1/2)min{s-1/4, 1/2-s} for 1/4<=s<=1/2,
         0 otherwise.                                         (10)

Its peak is 1/16 and its integral is 1/128. Consequently

    |kappa|=1,
    2 integral K=1/64,
    (1/4) integral (y_+-y_-)^2 d kappa=5/32,
    integral s^2 d eta - integral s^2 d nu=11/64.               (11)

The last equality is 1/64+5/32=11/64. Formula (9), including every sign,
can also be checked directly from the slope jumps of (10):
K''=(1/2)delta_(1/4)-delta_(3/8)+(1/2)delta_(1/2).

The PSD part is genuinely necessary for this target law. If all midpoint
terms were anchored at the original source (0,3/8), their pairs would
have to satisfy (a+b)/2=3/8. The negative endpoint target forces a=0,
so b would have to equal 3/4. The required positive endpoint law has
atoms only at 1/2 and 1; it has no atom at 3/4. Thus a pure anchored
midpoint decomposition at the original point is impossible, while the
horizontal PSD correction makes (9) exact.

This is an actual-face test of the decomposition, not an assertion that
(8) equals an actual critical cap derivative. The latter realization
would be an additional substantial condition.

## 7. What this resolves and what remains

Given the actual critical-roof convex-order coupling, the requested
three-layer representation by PSD continuous curvature and nonnegative
anchored lattice Jensen terms EXISTS; it need not be postulated as a new
lemma. Equations (3), (5), and (7) give its exact coefficients and budgets.
The ordinary triangle Euler charge corresponds to the first part alone;
the nonsymmetric test (8) requires both parts.

This does not make the OC constant follow. The archive already gives
examples where selected critical-cover convex order survives without a
Gamma-efficient individual group. Nothing in (1) bounds the midpoint
mass (5), the PSD trace, or their cap signatures by Gamma_d times the
original source volume. A further payment identity tied to actual cap
geometry, simultaneous menus, and the occupied parity budget is still
needed. The representation isolates where that identity would have to
act; it is not a functional restatement of OC and does not assume one.

The companion verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_three_layer_psd_midpoint_valuation_independent.py`
passes 63 exact mixed polynomial tests of (9), together with every variance
coefficient in (11). These finite checks supplement the distributional proof;
they are not the basis for its general validity.
